findings.evidence: Naming conventions, "Identifiers and theorem names": "Sometimes, to disambiguate the name of theorem or better convey the intended reference, it is necessary to describe some of the hypotheses. The word \"of\" is used to separate these hypotheses". Mathlib does exactly this for the same shape: `Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Subgroup/Pointwise.lean:105 closure_toSubmonoid` (unconditional) vs `Mathlib/GroupTheory/OrderOfElement.lean:855 Subgroup.closure_toSubmonoid_of_isOfFinOrder` and `:1135 closure_toSubmonoid_of_finite`; likewise `AddSubgroup.closure_eq_of_le` (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Span/Defs.lean:238).
findings.fix: Mark the hypothesis with `_of_`: e.g. `Subring.toAddSubgroup_closure_of_mul_mem` and `AddSubgroup.mul_mem_closure_of_mul_mem` (adjust the suffix to the hypothesis you prefer to name).
findings.issue: `Subring.toAddSubgroup_closure` names the equality `(Subring.closure s).toAddSubgroup = AddSubgroup.closure s`, which is false in general and holds only under the hypotheses `h1`/`hmul`; the name advertises the unconditional statement. Same problem at line 103: `AddSubgroup.mul_mem_closure` reads as `x, y ∈ closure s → x * y ∈ closure s`, false without the generator hypothesis `hs`.

summary: Naming is otherwise conclusion-describing and no notation is added; the earlier `choose` ambiguity is fixed. The two general closure helpers are named as unconditional facts although both are false without their extra hypothesis.
